params.body:
Two attempts did nothing. `public/_headers` deployed and the site kept answering with the two headers Netlify sends itself; a `[[headers]]` block in `netlify.toml` the same. Netlify's custom headers do not reach a response that comes from a function, and this site renders on the server: every request is a function.

So the headers go where the response is made: the middleware that was already there, with a rule that never overrides what the response already carries (Netlify sends a stronger HSTS of its own). And the two mechanisms that did nothing are removed: a file and a block that claim to do something they do not are worse than nothing.

After the deploy, `https://vlamingdam-frituur.netlify.app/beheer` should answer with referrer-policy and permissions-policy as well; Elixir judges the claim on exactly that.
params.title: De kopregels waar ze wel aankomen: in de middleware
